This allows you to shift profits around and reduce the taxable income in your home country.

**Transfer pricing** is another tool I use. By selling goods or services between your domestic business and your offshore subsidiaries at artificially low prices, you can move profits to the lower-tax jurisdiction. It's a way to inflate expenses and reduce taxable income, all while staying within the "spirit" of the law, if not always the letter.

**Consulting fees and advisory contracts** are also useful. By hiring yourself or your family members through a separate consulting firm, you can deduct those payments as business expenses. You're essentially paying yourself to "advise" your own company. It's a bit of a loop, but it's legal as long as the services are technically provided, even if they’re minimal.
